description: Poland KRZ National Debtor Registry Scraper. Automate bankruptcy and restructuring checks against the official public debtor registry. Nine search modes cover companies, persons, sole traders, case signatures, proceedings, shareholders, and assets. The bankruptcyEstate mode returns the trustee's filed estate inventory (spis masy upadlosci) for a company's proceedings - real estate, movables, cash, property rights and receivables, each with the trustee's own valuation, quantity and status. Pass entityName and/or identifier (proceedings are resolved for you) or a proceedingId; estateInventoryPublished:false means the register reports zero assets for that proceeding - a verified zero, not a failed lookup. For distressed-asset sourcing and creditor recovery-prospect assessment. Build a credit-risk watchlist or insolvency workflow. Pay-per-result. Advanced fields beyond this schema are also accepted (regdata_describe lists them).

advisorCity.description: Filter restructuring advisors by city. Only used in advisors mode.
advisorCity.title: Advisor City

caseSignature.description: Court case signature in format: CODE/REPERTORY/NUMBER/YEAR (e.g., WA1M/GU/223/2021). Used for signature and announcements modes.
caseSignature.title: Case Signature (Sygnatura)

dateFrom.description: Start date for announcement search (YYYY-MM-DD). Only used in announcements mode. A date range of up to 366 days is returned in full, even when it holds more than 1000 announcements; the run says so if a single day exceeds what the register will return.
dateFrom.title: Date From

dateTo.description: End date for announcement search (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. Only used in announcements mode. A malformed date, or a dateFrom after dateTo, stops the run before any search and nothing is charged.
dateTo.title: Date To

disableSessionCache.description: Advanced. By default the actor caches the KRZ guest token between your own runs (the token lives ~10h) so repeated/monitoring runs skip the slow browser bootstrap and run faster. The cache is private to your account and self-healing (a stale token is detected and refreshed automatically). Turn this on only to force a fresh session every run for debugging.
disableSessionCache.title: Disable session cache (advanced)

entityName.description: Company name, business name, or advisor surname (partial match). Used for entity, soleTrader, announcements, shareholders, bankruptcyEstate, and advisors modes.
entityName.title: Entity/Company Name

identifier.description: Entity identifier: KRS (10 digits), NIP, REGON. For persons: PESEL or NIP. For advisors: license number.
identifier.title: Identifier (KRS/NIP/REGON/PESEL)

maxItems.description: Optional cap on billed dataset items returned.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 100. Set to 0 for unlimited.
maxResults.title: Max Results

monitorKey.description: Just a label for your watchlist history, not a password or API key - it is shown masked. Optional name for this monitor's memory, e.g. 'client-acme'. Leave empty and the search itself is the name. Use it to keep two separate histories of the same search.
monitorKey.title: Monitor name (optional)

onlyNew.description: For scheduled checks of the same company or search. The first run returns everything and remembers it; every later run of the SAME search returns only proceedings that are new to it. Case-signature searches, where the register returns status and type, also report a status or type change (changeType, changedFields, previousValues); company-name searches carry no status, so they report new proceedings only. A run with nothing new succeeds with an empty dataset and a status message, and is billed like any search - 'nothing new' is the answer. The memory is kept in your own Apify account (a key-value store named regdata-krz-monitor); delete it to start again. Not available for proceedingDetails. Dates are not part of the memory, so a rolling announcements window keeps one history.
onlyNew.title: Monitor mode - only new or changed

proceedingId.description: Proceeding UUID (postepowanieId), as returned in the `proceedingId` field of an entity/person search. Used by searchMode 'proceedingDetails', and optionally by 'bankruptcyEstate' to read one specific estate.
proceedingId.title: Proceeding ID

proceedingKinds.description: Optional, entity mode only. A company search returns one row per proceeding the register holds for it. Keep only these kinds; leave empty for all. Left-out rows are not exported and not charged.
proceedingKinds.title: Proceeding kind filter (entity search)

proceedingType.description: Optional, announcements mode only. Keep only announcements of these proceeding types; leave empty for all. 'appeal' = second-instance rulings on a bankruptcy or restructuring case (e.g. on an arrangement or a repayment plan) - choosing 'restructuring' alone does NOT include appeal rulings on restructuring cases, so add 'appeal' too if you need them. Left-out rows are not exported and not charged.
proceedingType.title: Proceeding type filter (announcements)

searchMode.description: What to search for. 'entity' = companies by name/KRS/NIP. 'person' = natural persons by PESEL/NIP. 'soleTrader' = sole traders by name/identifier. 'signature' = by court case signature. 'announcements' = court announcements. 'shareholders' = partners in personal companies. 'bankruptcyEstate' = assets for sale from bankruptcy estates. 'advisors' = licensed restructuring advisors. 'proceedingDetails' = deep-dive into a specific proceeding.
searchMode.title: Search Mode
